title: Booking Systems & Money
summary: Splitwise, wallets, BookMyShow and libraries: modelling, money correctness and concurrency.

questions.q: Splitting ₹100.00 equally among 3 people. Which implementation is correct?
options: `double share = 100.0 / 3` for each person
Integer paise: 10000 / 3 = 3333 each, plus the remainder (1) to the first person, so the total is exactly 10000
Round each share to 2 decimals: 33.33 each
Charge 33.34 each and keep the extra
questions.explain: Shares must sum to the total exactly. Use integer minor units and distribute the remainder deterministically.

options: For performance only
A Seat is the physical chair in a screen's layout (catalogue). A ShowSeat is that chair's status and price for one specific show (inventory). Bookings change ShowSeats, never the layout
Java requires separate classes for each table
So premium seats can be subclasses
questions.explain: Catalogue vs inventory is the core modelling insight. The same pattern appears as Book/Copy and Product/StockItem.

questions.q: During `confirm`, the payment gateway takes up to 3 seconds. What's the concern with calling it while holding the show's lock?
options: None. Holding the lock guarantees correctness
Every other user of that show is blocked for 3 s. Production code marks the hold 'payment in progress' under the lock, calls the gateway outside it, then re-locks to apply the result
The gateway will deadlock
Java doesn't allow network calls in synchronized blocks
questions.explain: Never do slow or external I/O inside a critical section. State the trade-off even if your interview code keeps it simple.

questions.q: Two transfers run concurrently: A→B and B→A. Each locks the source account, then the destination. What happens, and what's the fix?
options: Nothing. Locks are reentrant
A possible deadlock (each holds one lock and waits for the other). Fix: always lock accounts in a global order such as ascending id
Money is duplicated. Use volatile
One transfer is lost. Use AtomicLong balances
questions.explain: A circular wait is the classic deadlock. Ordered locking removes it.

questions.q: A client times out on `transfer(500)` and retries. How do you make sure the user is charged once?
options: Check whether a transfer with the same amount happened in the last minute
Require an idempotency key. Store key → outcome atomically, and on a repeated key return the stored outcome without executing again
Ask the client not to retry
Use a distributed lock for the whole wallet
questions.explain: Idempotency keys are the standard answer. The check-and-store must be atomic for concurrent retries.

questions.q: Splitwise: A owes B 50 and B owes C 50. What does the greedy debt simplification produce?
options: A→C 50
C→A 50
Nothing, because it's already minimal
questions.explain: Net balances are A −50, B 0, C +50. Match the largest debtor with the largest creditor.

questions.q: Which data structure makes Splitwise's 'how much does X owe Y' and 'net balance of X' both simple?
options: A list of all expenses, recomputed on every query
An antisymmetric pairwise net map `net[a][b] = −net[b][a]`, updated on every expense and settlement
One balance per user only
A graph library
questions.explain: Pairwise netting handles 'A owes B 30, B owes A 10 → A owes B 20' for free, and balances are row sums. Keeping the expense list too is fine for history.

questions.q: Library: a member reserves a book with no free copy. When a copy is returned, what's the right behaviour?
options: Put it back on the shelf, available to anyone
Hold that copy for the first member in the reservation queue for a limited window and notify them. If they don't collect it, it becomes available
Automatically create a loan for the reserver
Reject the return until the reserver comes
questions.explain: A FIFO queue per book, a held state with lazy expiry, and an Observer-style notification.

questions.q: Two shows on the same screen: `[start1, end1)` and `[start2, end2)`. Which condition means they overlap?
options: `start1 == start2`
`start1 < end2 && start2 < end1`
`end1 < start2 || end2 < start1`
`start1 <= start2 <= end1`
questions.explain: The standard half-open interval overlap test. Option C is the *non*-overlap condition, inverted.

questions.q: Late fines are 'per day, capped at ₹500', and next year 'free for faculty'. How do you design for that?
options: Constants in the return method
A `FinePolicy` strategy injected into the library, so a faculty policy is a new implementation (or chosen per member type)
A subclass of Library for faculty
Store fines in the database and compute them in SQL
questions.explain: Rules that product managers will change belong behind an interface.
